correctness.rationale: A coordinate hyperdisk has support sqrt(1-u_j^2); convex-hull support takes the maximum and central symmetry doubles it. In 3D, conditional on |U_1|=s, the remaining angular fraction with both coordinates exceeding s in magnitude is 1-4 asin(s/sqrt(1-s^2))/pi; differentiation of the minimum-coordinate survival probability and an exact antiderivative give the CDF, zero at width 2sqrt(2/3) and one at width 2. For all d, squared coordinates have Dirichlet(1/2,...,1/2) density. Near equal squares 1/d, translated-simplex volume yields the explicit (d-1)-power lower tail; marginal coordinate density and pairwise O(t^2) overlap yield sqrt(epsilon) upper tail. Independent Gaussian minimum |Z| gives E after d scaling and LLN radial denominator gives (pi/2)E^2. Numerical quadrature independently recomputed four d=3 CDF values to 1e-12 and verified both endpoint formulas analytically.

value.rationale: PASS: Haar directional width is a natural probabilistic observable of a well-studied sparse-support convex body. An exact 3D law determines all quantiles, sharp all-dimensional endpoint powers describe rare extremal directions, and the d^3 high-dimensional limit records geometric anisotropy. These facts are distinct from known mean widths, volumes, radii and the classical support identity.

final_claim: For the convex hull of centered unit coordinate hyperdisks in R^d, Haar width equals 2 sqrt(1-min_j U_j^2). In d=3 it has an elementary exact CDF, in every d>=3 sharp lower/upper endpoint powers with explicit constants, and d^3(2-W_d) converges to (pi/2)Exp(1)^2.
limitations: Elementary CDF only d=3; in higher dimensions exact law is a Dirichlet integral plus asymptotics.
Fixed-d epsilon limits and growing-d weak limit are distinct regimes, not a joint uniform estimate.
residual_risks: The full generalized top-k norm primary article was not examined beyond its accessible abstract and scope.
A specialized older Dirichlet(1/2) minimum order-statistic source could contain the same integrated law.
